newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end sharply higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended sharply higher in a bounce from Friday's selloff and before key data on Tuesday.
Gains were timid early in the session, but stock index futures kept edging higher on short-covering into midday until intraday technicals accelerated gains, traders said.
U.S. June Standard and Poor's 500 futures triggered buy stops above 741.50 near midday, later poked above resistance at 744.50 and hit a new daily high at 748.20 in the final minutes of trade.
"It was a nice firm finish," a futures trader said.
One Wall Street firm was a featured buyer in the afternoon, and along with other firms the buyers easily absorbed the estimated 4,000 contracts a brokerage firm sold, traders said.

"They stalled at 743.90 and then they launched again," a trader for the brokerage firm said, noting buy stops above 744.00. Dealers "absorbed all the selling that I did and they bought into the close," he said.

Traders noted patches of aggressive buying on the rally, but said volume was only light to moderate overall. The Chicago Mercatile Exchange estimated Monday's overall S&P 500 volume at 78,963 contracts, down from 91,101 contracts traded on Friday.

"It was not very good volume, but it was also light on Friday's decline," another trader said. He said the market was edgy ahead of key inflation data Tuesday, when the March consumer price index is released at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT.

A Reuters poll of economists showed an average forecast for overall March CPI at up 0.2 percent, compared with up 0.3 percent in the previous report. The core rate -- prices excluding the volatile food and energy sectors -- was forecast up 0.3 percent versus up 0.2 percent in the previous report.
One trader said the market last week may have overdone the notion that core CPI would be strong and adjusted on Monday.
But one S&P trader called it an "up day in a downtrend" and said the overall bent was for continued weakness.
Still, some traders after the close said they were encouraged by first-quarter Intel earnings, at $2.20 a share.

At the close, June S&P 500s were up 8.80 points at 747.30, Nasdaq 100s rallied 18.85 points to 815.85, Russell 2000s were up 1.25 points at 341.35, KCBT Value Line futures rose 3.70 points to 681.40, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 50.0 to 17,740.0 and Midcap 400s gained 2.80 points to 252.10.
